$comment: Values emitted from docs/design/design-system.manifest.json that no component reads. `scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs` fails on any emitted name that is neither read nor listed here, AND on any name listed here that a component does read — both directions, because a dead exemption is how a live one gets waved through later. Every entry carries a `why` and a `cites`, and the whole list PRINTS ON EVERY RUN rather than only on a failure: an exemption nobody reads is an exemption nobody weighs. Same shape as retired-surface.json. See F-092 and .harness/plans/F-092-a-token-that-reaches-no-pixel.md.
$groupComment: `group` is required because `xs` is a radius step AND a type step, and they are not the same decision. One of them is read by 22 `size="xs"` literals; the other is read by nothing.
$readingComment: This file is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT. If it grows without anyone reading it, the citations are what makes that visible — an entry nobody can justify shows up as an entry with a weak one.

unreached.why: The web target. apps/mobile is the only surface (ADR-0051), so nothing in the reader zone imports these — their only reader is emit.test.ts, which is precisely the case this check reports. They are emitted anyway because four targets from one manifest is what stops web and mobile drifting the day a web surface exists (ADR-0020). Deleting them would remove the guarantee, not the dead code. JUDGEABLE_SAMPLE joins them for F-151 and is the same case exactly: its mobile twin `nativeJudgeableSample` is read by `Pair` and `Strip`, and the CSS variable beside it is emitted for the same reason the other three web bindings are. It is worth saying what it IS, because it is the one value here that is derived rather than declared: the smallest a sample may be drawn where a screen asks you to JUDGE a colour, computed from the CIE 2° standard observer at the declared viewing distance — the same observer this product’s colorimetry uses everywhere and the one ΔE00 is parameterised for (ADR-0095). A web surface that drew a sample smaller than this would be making the mistake the mobile one no longer can.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0051 — the web target exists so four targets cannot drift

unreached.why: Emitted to CONSTRAIN, not to paint. TEXT_TOKENS is read only through its derived `TextToken` type, which is what stops `foreground.3` compiling below the large-text floor in Text.tsx. The other three are read in real code only by packages/ui/src/testing/conformance.ts, which this check deliberately does not count as a reader — that exclusion is what makes acceptance criterion 2 mean anything. A value whose job is to be checked against is a real value with no pixel, and that difference belongs here where it can be read rather than inferred. DECLARED_PAIRINGS joins them for F-171 and is the clearest case of the kind: it is the manifest pairsWith graph, emitted so the conformance suite can ask whether a pair it just found RENDERED is one gate 9 has an opinion about. Gate 9 checks the pairings the manifest declares; the suite checks that every painted colour resolves to a token; neither of them looked at a pair on a screen, so a component could draw two perfectly good tokens in a combination nothing had ever measured — and one did, 546 times. A component will never read this value, because reading it would be a component deciding whether its own colours are allowed.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0054 — emitted to constrain the type, never to paint

unreached.why: THE FOUR PRE-COMPOSITED FORMS, and what is left of an entry that also held `border` itself. F-156 painted the hairline: the accordion on the colour page draws a rule between its reference sections, which is the first line in this product that SEPARATES without BOUNDING. That distinction is why the entry stood for so long — every component that drew a line reached for `border.strong`, the boundary of an outlined control where WCAG 1.4.11 applies directly and 3:1 is not optional, and this product had no row list to put a decorative rule between. F-143 was the previous owner and did not close it, which was worth stating plainly rather than quietly re-assigning: its popover panel is an outlined surface and took `border.strong` like everything before it. THESE FOUR ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND RATHER THAN IN SCHEDULE, which is why they take `closedBy: null`. They are the values the CONTRAST GATE composited so it could measure a translucent token against each ground it may sit on — an rgba() has no contrast ratio until something is behind it. A component never reads one: it reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite. No surface will ever paint them, so no feature can close this.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0044 — the .on.* forms are what the contrast gate measured, not what a component reads: a component reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite it. No surface will ever paint them. `border` itself was the schedulable half of this entry and F-156 closed it.

unreached.why: THE FOUR PRE-COMPOSITED FORMS, and what is left of an entry that also held `backdrop` itself. F-143 painted the scrim: `Popover.Overlay` takes `backdrop`, which is the first time anything in this product dimmed the page behind something — the old reason read "there is no dialog, bottom sheet or modal anywhere in the app yet", and now there is. THESE FOUR ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND RATHER THAN IN SCHEDULE, which is why they take `closedBy: null`. `backdrop.on.background` and its siblings are the values the CONTRAST GATE composited so it could measure a translucent token against each ground it may sit on — an rgba() has no contrast ratio until something is behind it. A component never reads one: it reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite. No surface will ever paint them, so no feature can close this.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0044 — the .on.* forms are what the contrast gate measured, not what a component reads: a component reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite it. No surface will ever paint them.

unreached.why: ONE OF THREE, AND THE REASON CHANGED KIND IN F-174 — `warn` is no longer BLOCKED, it is UNUSED, and those are different facts. The previous reason said the obvious home for it, a status beside a colour sample, was closed: `Status` takes `adjacentToSample`, which puts it on `swatch.well`, and light `warn` measured 4.32:1 there against a floor of 4.5. ADR-0098 moved all three light status tokens and `warn` now measures 4.75:1 on that ground, declared and checked in all eight palettes. THE OBSTACLE IS GONE AND THE READER IS STILL MISSING. F-152 gave `bad` and `ok` theirs — the refused photograph on AddGarment and the failed and successful writes on Export — and nothing since has had a middle outcome to report. THE PREVIOUS OWNERS OF THIS ENTRY WERE WRONG TWICE AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING VISIBLE: it first said outfit scoring (F-031) would show the first status, and F-031 shipped without one; it then said F-149 would, and F-149 REMOVED the only reader `warn` had, because its own criterion asks for one calm readout rather than three warnings. So this entry names no feature this time. A caution is a judgement — "this is probably fine, but" — and this product is deliberately built to describe rather than judge (the Lens, ADR-0031, the measurement-claims policy). The token stays because the day a surface has a genuine middle outcome it must not have to invent a colour for it, and because a two-state status system would make every non-failure look identical.
unreached.permanentBecause: Not permanent in the sense the `.on.*` entries are — a surface COULD reach it. Permanent in the sense that no feature can be scheduled to close it: naming one is what went wrong twice already, and a caution needs a product moment rather than an owner. Re-read this the first time a screen has an outcome that is neither success nor failure.
